beats.text: Most couples don't meet through friends anymore!
Friends used to be the top matchmaker. That's not how most couples start anymore.
Stanford researchers asked thousands of American couples one question: how did you meet?
In nineteen ninety-five, friends were the top matchmaker. Thirty-three percent. By twenty seventeen, just twenty. So who took over?
The internet! From two percent to thirty-nine. Now the most common way couples meet.
So if you met your partner on an app? You're not the weird story. You're the normal one!

sources: Rosenfeld, Thomas & Hausen (2019), 'Disintermediating your friends: How online dating in the United States displaces other ways of meeting', PNAS 116(36), 17753-17758. HCMST 2009 + 2017 surveys, 5,421 heterosexual couples (Table 1). Met online: 2% (1995) -> 39% (2017); met through friends: 33% (1995) -> 20% (2017). Via PMC6731751 / Stanford News (Aug 2019).
